hero.headline: White House to launch children's investment accounts on July 4
hero.body:
The Trump administration plans to introduce investment accounts for children on July 4, positioning the initiative as a way to strengthen the financial prospects of millions of Americans under 18. The program, branded as "Trump Accounts," will be available to children who have not yet turned 18 by the end of the calendar year.

The announcement represents a significant policy move from the administration, though specific details about implementation remain limited. The White House has not yet clarified how the accounts will be funded, what investment options families can choose, or the process for accessing them. The July 4 launch date coincides with Independence Day celebrations across the country.

This federal investment account program marks a departure from existing child savings initiatives. While some states and localities have developed similar programs in recent years, this is the first nationally administered investment account program specifically designed for children.

The initiative aligns with the administration's broader push to expand wealth-building opportunities for American families. As the launch date approaches, lawmakers and policy analysts are expected to scrutinize the program's structure, including contribution limits, tax implications, and administrative oversight.

Several key questions remain unanswered about the program's design. The administration has not disclosed whether the accounts will be available universally to all eligible children or limited to families meeting certain income thresholds. Details about eligibility requirements beyond age have not been provided.

The long-term effectiveness of these accounts will depend significantly on factors the administration has not yet made public. These include initial funding amounts, potential for investment growth, and any restrictions on withdrawals before children reach adulthood.

House Democrats have criticized the timing and structure of the announcement. A 55-page report from House Democrats accuses the administration of using America's 250th birthday celebration for political gain, pointing to fundraising methods they describe as questionable. Watchdog groups have previously raised concerns about these practices.

The administration has framed the accounts as providing young Americans with a financial advantage early in life. Officials suggest the program will help build wealth among the nation's youth, though they have not yet released the detailed information necessary to assess how effectively it might achieve this goal.

Further implementation details are expected as the July 4 rollout date approaches. The administration's release of these specifics will likely shape the policy debate among lawmakers, economists, and advocacy groups interested in child welfare and financial inclusion programs.

cards.headline: US and Iran hold separate talks in Qatar on Strait of Hormuz tensions
cards.teaser: Negotiations between US and Iranian officials paused for the funeral of a senior ayatollah after mediators reported progress on reducing tensions.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators met separately in Qatar on Wednesday with Qatari and Pakistani mediators present. According to Qatar's statement, positive progress was made during the discussions, and both sides agreed to continue their dialogue.

The talks paused to allow Iranian officials to attend funeral services for a senior ayatollah. The negotiations represent an effort to establish communication channels between Washington and Tehran amid regional tensions.

cards.headline: Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv kills at least 27
cards.body:
Russia launched what officials described as the largest weapons assault on Kyiv in over four years of war, killing at least 27 people and injuring dozens more. The overnight attack deployed nearly 500 drones and more than 70 missiles across the capital and other parts of the country in the early hours of Thursday.

Explosions rocked Kyiv for several hours as successive waves of cruise and ballistic missiles arrived, with the city's air defense systems working to intercept incoming projectiles. Fires burned across multiple locations after dawn broke, with strikes and debris hitting residential buildings in several districts and a hotel on a central boulevard. In one area on the left bank of the Dnipro River, a large section of a nine-story apartment block was destroyed and reduced to rubble. Rescue workers continued searching through the remains throughout the day, with the death toll rising as the search progressed.

About 70 people were admitted to hospitals, and more than 50,000 residents took shelter in metro stations after President Volodymyr Zelensky warned on Wednesday that a massive attack was imminent. Some people brought mattresses and tents to sleep below ground as platforms filled with hundreds seeking safety.

Zelensky returned early from a trip to Ireland to visit attack sites in Kyiv on Thursday afternoon. He said that if allies had supplied the air defense missiles they had promised, the damage would have been significantly less. "We are fighting alone. The victims are only Ukrainians. All we ask from our partners is that they do what they agreed to," he said.

The Russian defense ministry claimed the strikes targeted military facilities and energy infrastructure, stating the attacks were retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries. However, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha rejected this characterization, calling it "immoral" to equate an aggressor with a country defending itself. He emphasized that Ukraine has the right to strike legitimate military targets in Russia.

Ukraine has intensified long-range drone strikes against oil refineries in Russia in recent weeks, causing fuel shortages across the country. Multiple Russian regions have introduced petrol rationing, while Russian-occupied Crimea declared a state of emergency.

The attack prompted NATO ally Poland to scramble fighter jets as a preventive measure, while Finland briefly issued a temporary aviation restriction zone in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer called the attacks "a stark reminder that while Ukraine continues to pursue peace, Putin continues to inflict suffering and violence on the Ukrainian people." Zelensky indicated his national security council secretary had been in contact with US negotiator Jared Kushner in recent days regarding peace efforts.

cards.headline: Trump EPA issues guidance departing from Biden report on contaminated farmland cancer risks
cards.teaser: The Environmental Protection Agency criticized a draft Biden administration assessment on health hazards from contaminated sludge applied to farmland.
cards.body:
The Environmental Protection Agency this week issued draft guidance that criticizes a Biden administration risk assessment on health hazards from applying contaminated sludge to farmland. The Biden-era assessment had examined human health risks, including cancer, from farms contaminated with forever chemicals—persistent substances that don't break down in the environment or the body.

The new guidance reflects the Trump administration's different regulatory approach to forever chemical contamination in agricultural settings, signaling a shift in how it addresses health risks associated with these chemicals in the food supply.

cards.headline: Colorado wildfire expands past 50,000 acres as hundreds evacuate
cards.body:
A fast-moving wildfire in southern Colorado has grown to more than 50,000 acres, forcing hundreds of residents to evacuate as the blaze became the top firefighting priority in the United States. The Aspen Acres fire has doubled in size as it continues to spread through the region.

Evacuation notices have expanded as crews work to contain the fire. The blaze destroyed a bridge on Colorado Highway 165 south of Beulah, which the Colorado Department of Transportation rebuilt in 11 hours to maintain access for emergency crews and evacuating residents.

The rapid growth of the fire has prompted officials to designate it as the number one priority fire in the state. Fire crews from across the region have been deployed to combat the blaze as it continues to threaten communities in southern Colorado.

The fire represents a significant threat to both populated areas and the surrounding landscape. Hundreds of residents have been ordered to leave their homes as the fire continues its expansion. Emergency management officials are monitoring conditions closely as they coordinate response efforts.

The Aspen Acres fire is part of a larger crisis unfolding across the western United States. Thousands of firefighters have been deployed across western states and Alaska to fight multiple wildfires this month, fueled by dry, hot weather and high winds. Both Utah and Colorado governors have declared states of emergency in response to dangerous conditions.

The situation has become increasingly dire for firefighting crews. The US Department of Interior released the names of three firefighters killed while working to contain wildfires along the Utah-Colorado border. Emily Barker of Michigan, Nick Hutcherson of Arizona, and Sydney Watson of Alabama were killed on Saturday while fighting the Knowles fire in western Colorado. Two other firefighters from their specialized helicopter-deployed crew were also injured.

The crew attempted to use tent-like shelters to protect themselves from the flames but were overcome by the fire. The Knowles fire they were fighting has since merged with two other fires to form the Snyder Mesa fire, which has burned over 28,000 acres.

Colorado Governor Jared Polis issued a statement mourning the deaths, saying "The men and women who serve on the frontlines of these fires risk their lives to keep us safe and to protect the lands and communities we love." He noted that the state was working with the Bureau of Land Management, Colorado National Guard, and other officials to fight the fires and recover the bodies.

The Department of Interior has mobilized a serious accident investigation team to review the circumstances of the incident. Forest Service Deputy Chief Sarah Fisher said in a statement that "This is an incredibly difficult moment for the entire wildland fire community. Our heavy hearts are with the families during this unimaginable time."

cards.headline: Energy Department Orders Data Centers to Reduce Grid Usage During Heat Wave
cards.teaser: Federal officials directed data centers to tap backup power sources as a brutal heat wave strains the electrical grid from Washington to Boston.
cards.body:
The Department of Energy has directed data centers to reduce their electrical grid consumption and rely on backup power during a severe heat wave sweeping the eastern United States. Record-breaking temperatures are affecting major cities from Washington, D.C., to Boston, with even hotter conditions expected Friday.

The PJM power grid, which supplies electricity to 65 million people across 13 states, activated emergency protocols to manage the strain. Data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity to cool servers and maintain operations, putting additional pressure on grids during periods of peak demand. The directive marks an unusual federal intervention into private sector operations aimed at stabilizing the power system.

cards.headline: Planned Parenthood to regain federal Medicaid funding as Republican ban expires
cards.teaser: The health care organization will regain access to federal funding on Saturday, one year after being cut off from Medicaid under Republican legislation.
cards.body:
Planned Parenthood will regain access to federal funding on Saturday, one year after Republicans cut its clinics off from Medicaid. Republicans successfully used the party-line One Big Beautiful Bill Act last year to achieve their goal of defunding Planned Parenthood.

The complicated Senate rules involved in passing that legislation meant the ban had a limited duration. The expiration of the funding prohibition returns Planned Parenthood clinics to their previous status as eligible Medicaid providers, reversing a policy change that had been a priority for Republican lawmakers.

cards.headline: Pope excommunicates traditionalist bishops after unsanctioned ordinations
cards.teaser: The Vatican excommunicated bishops of the Society of St. Pius X after the group consecrated new bishops without papal approval.
cards.body:
The Vatican declared the Society of St. Pius X in schism and excommunicated its bishops and priests after the traditionalist group consecrated new bishops without papal approval. The move marks a major crisis for Pope Leo XIV's papacy.

The Society of St. Pius X, also known as the Lefebvrites, has long disputed Rome's authority over theological and liturgical matters. The organization maintains Catholic practices that predate the Second Vatican Council's reforms. The excommunication followed the group's decision to proceed with episcopal consecrations despite explicit papal warnings against doing so.

cards.headline: US and Iran hold separate talks in Qatar on Strait of Hormuz tensions
cards.teaser: Negotiations between US and Iranian officials paused for the funeral of a senior ayatollah after mediators reported progress on reducing tensions.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators met separately in Qatar on Wednesday with Qatari and Pakistani mediators present. According to Qatar's statement, positive progress was made during the discussions, and both sides agreed to continue their dialogue.

The talks paused to allow Iranian officials to attend funeral services for a senior ayatollah. The negotiations represent an effort to establish communication channels between Washington and Tehran amid regional tensions.

cards.headline: Explosion at Damascus cafe kills nine people
cards.teaser: A bomb blast at a crowded cafe in central Damascus killed at least nine people and injured at least 20 others.
cards.body:
An explosion at a cafe in central Damascus killed at least nine people, according to Syrian state media. The blast struck a establishment near the Palace of Justice, a major government building, during what appeared to be a busy time.

No group has claimed responsibility for the bombing. The attack marks a rare incident of violence in the Syrian capital in recent months.

cards.headline: Ebola treatment trial launches in Democratic Republic of Congo
cards.teaser: Health officials began testing treatments for Ebola as the disease has caused 438 deaths among nearly 1,700 confirmed and suspected cases.
cards.body:
A clinical trial for Ebola treatments has begun in the Democratic Republic of Congo during an ongoing outbreak. The World Health Organization has documented 1,406 confirmed cases of the disease, along with 301 suspected cases and 438 deaths.

The trial will test the effectiveness of various treatment approaches for patients infected with the virus. Health workers are conducting the research while simultaneously managing containment efforts to prevent further spread across affected regions.

cards.headline: UK lawmakers call for deportation of grooming gang leader
cards.teaser: British parliamentarians are demanding the deportation of Shabir Ahmed, who received a lengthy prison sentence in 2012 for leading a sexual exploitation ring.
cards.body:
Members of Parliament are pushing for the deportation of Shabir Ahmed, who was sentenced to a lengthy prison term in 2012 for his role in organizing a sexual exploitation ring. Ahmed was convicted for his involvement in a grooming gang that targeted vulnerable victims.

The calls for deportation come as his sentence nears completion. UK law allows for the removal of foreign nationals convicted of serious crimes after they serve their sentences. Lawmakers arguing for deportation cite the severity of his crimes and the impact on victims as justification for removal from the country.

cards.headline: Pickup truck crashes into Buddhist procession in Thailand, killing nine monks
cards.teaser: A boy driving a pickup truck struck a group of Buddhist monks on pilgrimage in northeast Thailand, killing nine and injuring 11 others.
cards.body:
An 11-year-old boy drove his parents' truck into a Buddhist procession in Mukdahan, northeast Thailand, killing at least nine monks and injuring 11 others. The group of 35 monks and five lay followers were walking by the roadside when the vehicle struck them. CCTV footage captured the moment the monks in orange robes were hit as they traveled along the road on Thursday morning.

Police are investigating the circumstances of the collision. No charges have been filed against the child as authorities work to establish what led to the crash.

cards.headline: Louisiana attorney general indicted by grand jury
cards.teaser: A grand jury has indicted Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill in connection with a dispute over changes to local courts.
cards.body:
Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill, a Republican, has been indicted on criminal charges by a grand jury in New Orleans. She is accused of attempting to intimidate local officials who opposed a GOP-enacted law overhauling the local court system.

Murrill allegedly told eight New Orleans officials, including Mayor Helena Moreno and District Attorney Jason Williams, that they could lose their jobs because of their opposition to the legislation. The indictment represents a significant legal challenge for the state's top law enforcement official.

cards.headline: Texas governor appoints Don Huffines as state comptroller
cards.teaser: Texas Governor Greg Abbott has appointed Don Huffines, a former hard right critic, to serve as the state's comptroller.
cards.body:
Governor Abbott selected Huffines for the state's top finance position. Huffines had previously been a critic from the right wing of the Republican Party before receiving the appointment to oversee Texas finances.

The appointment comes as acting Comptroller Kelly Hancock prepares to step down from the role of Texas chief financial officer at the end of July. Hancock had been leading the state's school voucher rollout before announcing plans to leave the position.

cards.headline: House Democrats allege donors misled by Trump-backed Freedom 250
cards.teaser: House Democrats have released a report alleging that donors were misled by the organizer of America's 250th birthday events, which received backing from former President Trump.
cards.body:
A 55-page report from House Democrats accuses Freedom 250, the Trump-backed organizer of America's 250th anniversary celebrations, of misleading donors through questionable fundraising methods. The report alleges the organization prioritized profit over authentic commemorations.

Democrats contend that Trump used the semiquincentennial events to advance political ideology and personal interests rather than create unifying national celebrations. Watchdog groups had previously raised concerns about the organization's practices.

cards.headline: Couple charged after staging proposal atop Empire State Building
cards.teaser: Two people who climbed to the top of the Empire State Building for an apparent proposal face multiple charges after being arrested and released from jail.
cards.body:
Angela Nikolau and Ivan Beerkus were taken into custody after scaling the Empire State Building in New York City, where they staged what appeared to be an engagement. The couple, known as daredevils, reached the top of the iconic skyscraper without authorization.

The pair were arraigned on multiple charges following their arrest. They have since been released from jail as the case proceeds. The incident drew attention both for the security breach it represented and the couple's public display at one of New York's most recognizable landmarks.

cards.headline: Former Olympian indicted over alleged Reflecting Pool vandalism
cards.teaser: A former Olympic canoeist has been indicted on a felony charge after allegedly damaging Washington's Reflecting Pool.
cards.body:
David Hearn, a three-time US Olympic canoeist, has been indicted by a Washington DC grand jury for allegedly damaging the Reflecting Pool's liner on June 19. The 67-year-old was arrested after touching a peeling section of material from the pool's $14.7 million renovation project.

The indictment charges Hearn with maliciously breaking or destroying lining material. His legal team has disputed the allegations, arguing that the Trump administration is treating ordinary conduct as criminal activity.

cards.headline: Rare copy of Declaration of Independence discovered in UK archives
cards.teaser: A volunteer discovered a rare copy of the United States Declaration of Independence in archives in the United Kingdom.
cards.body:
The newly found copy is one of only 11 surviving versions of the "Exeter printing" of the Declaration of Independence known to exist. It is also the only copy of this particular printing known to be outside the United States. The document was discovered in late May by Michael Scurr, a volunteer cataloguing previously unrecorded materials at the National Archives in Kew, west London. He recognized the opening words while examining a volume of 18th-century Royal Navy correspondence.

The Declaration, adopted on July 4, 1776, exists in very few original copies. This particular version was taken from an American privateer ship, making its presence in UK archives a significant historical find that adds to the small number of authenticated versions of this founding document that have survived for nearly 250 years.

hero.headline: Meta Explores Cloud Computing Business as Stock Fluctuates
hero.teaser: Meta is pursuing entry into the cloud computing market, prompting mixed reactions from investors and analysts concerned about potential margin impacts.
hero.body:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is exploring launching a cloud computing business, joining other tech companies seeking to become what industry analysts call neoclouds. The move initially sent Meta stock higher but shares later fell as investors considered immediate challenges to the plan. Wall Street analysts warned that entering cloud computing would likely mean lower profit margins for the company.

The announcement comes at a pivotal moment for the tech industry. Three of Meta's peers among the most valuable publicly traded companies in the world, Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft, all reported double-digit gains in their cloud computing divisions during their latest quarterly earnings. These cloud services have experienced accelerated growth driven by increased adoption of artificial intelligence. Meta, which does not currently operate a cloud computing business, failed to meet Wall Street expectations during its earnings report.

The four companies have collectively planned to spend 650 billion dollars in 2026 on AI infrastructure. Both Alphabet and Meta revised their capital expenditure projections upward. Alphabet's revenue gains appeared to calm investor concerns, but Meta's announcement that it would increase its capital expenditures from a 115 billion dollar minimum to 125 billion dollars triggered a stock decline of over 5 percent in after-hours trading.

Alphabet reported 63 percent year-on-year growth for Google Cloud. CEO Sundar Pichai stated that 2026 is off to a strong start, with the company's AI investment beginning to deliver returns. All four companies framed their results as evidence that their AI integration and infrastructure development strategy was working.

Meta reported 56.31 billion dollars in revenue, exceeding the expected 55.45 billion dollars. The company also revealed a more than 7 percent increase in its projected capital expenditure for the year. During the earnings call, Zuckerberg denied that artificial intelligence would replace humans, saying instead that it would amplify people's ability to do what they want. He stated that Meta was on track to deliver personal super-intelligence to billions of people.

The broader tech industry is undergoing significant workforce reductions linked to AI adoption. Meta announced layoffs of 10 percent of its staff, about 8,000 employees. Microsoft offered voluntary retirement packages to approximately 125,000 workers. Amazon cut nearly 10 percent of its corporate workforce, about 30,000 employees.

The industry has long faced questions about when its massive spending and intense focus on artificial intelligence would generate returns. This earnings season appeared to provide a clear answer: revenue growth from cloud computing services powered by artificial intelligence. Meta's potential entry into cloud computing would place it in direct competition with established providers like Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud.

cards.headline: Nasdaq Falls After June Hiring Report Misses Expectations
cards.teaser: Stock indexes moved in opposite directions Thursday as the Nasdaq declined while the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped nearly 600 points to a record close.
cards.body:
The Nasdaq declined Thursday following a weaker-than-expected June employment report. Semiconductor stocks led the losses, while the S&P 500 also fell as Tesla shares sank. By contrast, the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged nearly 600 points to close at a record high, reflecting what analysts describe as a rotation trade across different market sectors.

The divergent performance highlights investor shifting between sectors and growing focus on labor market conditions. Market observers expect worker-related economic indicators to drive trading patterns through the remainder of 2026.

cards.headline: Trump Criticizes Federal Reserve Board as New Chair Warsh Takes Office
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump publicly criticized the Federal Reserve Board on Thursday, describing it as hostile to newly appointed Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said Thursday that newly appointed Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh faces a board that is "a little bit hostile," while acknowledging that Warsh "has to do what he has to do" on interest rates. The comments mark Trump's latest public intervention in Federal Reserve policy, traditionally kept separate from presidential influence.

Trump has previously expressed frustration with Fed decisions on interest rates, citing their impact on economic growth. The Federal Reserve Board's seven governors serve 14-year terms specifically designed to insulate monetary policy from political pressure. Though board members are nominated by the president and confirmed by the Senate, they operate independently once appointed.

cards.teaser: Federal officials directed data centers to tap backup power sources as a brutal heat wave strains the electrical grid from Washington to Boston.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Egg Producers Settle Price-Fixing Lawsuit for $3.3 Million
cards.teaser: Companies agreed to pay damages and donate more than 53 million eggs to food banks in 17 states that joined the federal antitrust action.
cards.body:
Egg producers have agreed to pay $3.3 million to resolve federal antitrust allegations brought by the government and 17 states. The settlement addresses claims that the companies engaged in anticompetitive practices that artificially raised egg prices.

As part of the agreement, the producers will donate more than 53 million eggs to food banks and nonprofit organizations across the participating states. The settlement represents government action against alleged collusion in the food industry.

cards.headline: Tesla Stock Falls 7% Despite Beating Delivery Forecasts
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker reported 480,000 second-quarter deliveries, topping estimates, but shares posted their worst day in nearly a year.
cards.body:
Tesla shares declined 7% on Thursday, marking the worst single-day performance in nearly a year, even as the company reported stronger-than-expected vehicle deliveries. The automaker delivered 480,000 vehicles in the second quarter, surpassing analyst expectations and achieving a 3% increase with a notable rebound in European sales.

The stock decline followed a 12% weekly gain leading up to the delivery announcement. Investors appeared to take profits after the report despite Tesla's positive operational results. The European recovery represents a bright spot as global car sales growth has slowed industrywide.

cards.headline: Zuckerberg Says AI Agent Development Moving Slower Than Expected
cards.teaser: The Meta CEO told staff that artificial intelligence agent technology has not progressed as quickly as he had hoped.
cards.body:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg told employees that AI agent technology is developing slower than he expected. The admission came shortly after Meta laid off 8,000 workers in early morning emails. Zuckerberg suggested that focusing on core technological development could improve the job situation at the company.

AI agents are software programs designed to perform tasks independently for users. Meta has made substantial investments in artificial intelligence research and infrastructure, making the slower-than-anticipated progress significant. Zuckerberg's comments to staff indicate the company may need to revise its timeline for launching agent-based AI products.

hero.headline: James Webb telescope detects planet that survived its star's death
hero.body:
Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope have observed a planet orbiting a white dwarf star, providing insights into what could happen to planets in our solar system when the sun eventually dies. The discovery marks an important milestone in studying worlds that have endured the catastrophic transformation of their host stars.

The planet contains aerosols and hydrocarbons in its atmosphere, according to findings published in Nature. White dwarfs are the dense remnants left behind after stars like our sun exhaust their nuclear fuel and shed their outer layers in violent explosions. This process typically destroys nearby planets or ejects them from their systems entirely.

The survival of this particular world despite such extreme conditions challenges previous assumptions about planetary survival. When stars evolve into red giants before collapsing into white dwarfs, they expand dramatically and can engulf planets orbiting close to them. The fact that this planet persisted through this transformation suggests it either maintained a distant orbit or migrated inward after the star's death was complete.

The atmospheric composition detected by the Webb telescope provides valuable clues about how planets can survive such catastrophic stellar events. The presence of complex molecules indicates the planet retained or reformed an atmosphere following its star's collapse. Researchers from the European Space Agency participated in analyzing the observational data.

This discovery carries significant implications for understanding the long-term fate of our own solar system. In approximately five billion years, the sun will enter its red giant phase before eventually becoming a white dwarf. Planets in the inner solar system, including Earth, face probable destruction during this transformation. The outer planets may survive in fundamentally altered orbits around the sun's white dwarf remnant, though their conditions would change dramatically as the dying star's energy output diminishes.

The observations represent a rare opportunity to study how planetary atmospheres behave during and after stellar death. Scientists can now examine whether planets maintain their atmospheric compositions through such violent processes or acquire new ones afterward. The complex molecules detected suggest that planetary systems remain more resilient than previously thought.

Understanding these survival mechanisms helps astronomers predict what might happen to exoplanetary systems across the galaxy. Many white dwarf systems likely harbor planets that survived their host stars' deaths, making them important subjects for continued observation. The James Webb Space Telescope's capabilities allow researchers to analyze atmospheric details that would be impossible to detect with previous instruments.

As humanity grapples with the ultimate fate of Earth and its neighboring planets, observations like these provide sobering yet fascinating glimpses into the distant future. While the timeline extends billions of years into the future, understanding these processes now helps scientists prepare for the realities our solar system will eventually face.

cards.headline: Meta CEO says AI agent development slower than expected
cards.teaser: Mark Zuckerberg told staff that AI development efforts have not progressed as quickly as anticipated.
cards.body:
Mark Zuckerberg addressed Meta employees at an internal meeting about the pace of AI agent development. The CEO said that efforts to advance AI systems were moving slower than the company had hoped.

The comments reflect the challenges technology companies face in delivering on ambitious AI promises. Meta has invested heavily in artificial intelligence development as part of its broader technology strategy.

cards.headline: Private companies fly military satellite missions for Space Force
cards.teaser: True Anomaly and Rocket Lab are conducting satellite fly-by operations for the U.S. military.
cards.body:
The U.S. Space Force has contracted private space companies to perform orbital missions involving satellite maneuvers. True Anomaly and Rocket Lab are executing the operations, which resemble aerial combat training exercises adapted for space.

The missions involve satellites conducting close approaches to other spacecraft in orbit. The military application represents an expansion of commercial space capabilities into national security operations.

cards.headline: European quantum computing company goes public with uncertain outlook
cards.teaser: IQM acknowledged uncertainty about quantum technology's future as it listed on Nasdaq at a $1.9 billion valuation.
cards.body:
IQM, a Finnish quantum computing company, made its public market debut on Nasdaq with a valuation of approximately $1.9 billion, marking a milestone as Europe's first publicly traded quantum firm.

The company develops full-stack quantum computing systems. Like others in the emerging quantum sector, IQM faces significant technical and commercial hurdles as the industry works toward practical applications.

cards.headline: New macOS malware discovered with unusual characteristics
cards.teaser: Security researchers found PamStealer, an infostealer targeting Mac computers with different techniques than typical malware.
cards.body:
Cybersecurity researchers identified a new malware strain called PamStealer designed to steal information from macOS computers. The malware exhibits characteristics that differ from typical Mac infostealers currently in circulation.

The discovery highlights increased attention from malware developers toward Apple's operating system. Mac users have historically faced fewer malware threats than Windows users, but security researchers report growing sophistication in attacks targeting macOS.

cards.headline: AI energy demands complicate tech companies' climate commitments
cards.teaser: Google and Amazon face challenges meeting net-zero emissions pledges as AI operations increase energy consumption.
cards.body:
Artificial intelligence systems have increased energy consumption at major technology companies, making climate goals harder to achieve. Amazon and Google both committed to reaching net-zero carbon emissions but face obstacles as AI workloads expand.

Data centers running AI models require substantially more electricity than traditional computing operations. The energy intensity of training and operating large AI systems has grown as companies deploy more powerful models across their services.

cards.headline: Rocksteady developers say game failure led to burnout
cards.teaser: Senior developers on Suicide Squad said the game's commercial failure made them question continuing in the industry.
cards.body:
Key developers at Rocksteady Studios discussed the impact of Suicide Squad's poor commercial performance on their careers. The designers said the experience of working on the unsuccessful live service game left them feeling burned out and reconsidering their futures in game development.

One developer warned that the video game industry has lost direction in its approach to game design. The comments reflect broader concerns about the sustainability of large-scale game development and the shift toward live service models.

hero.headline: Billy Donovan joins Spurs as lead assistant coach
hero.teaser: The veteran coach agreed to become the top assistant for head coach Mitch Johnson in San Antonio.
hero.body:
Billy Donovan has agreed to become the lead assistant coach for the San Antonio Spurs and head coach Mitch Johnson, sources told ESPN. The move brings the experienced coach to San Antonio's staff in a senior role.

Donovan previously served as a head coach in the NBA and at the college level before taking the assistant position. His hiring adds veteran coaching experience to Johnson's staff as the Spurs continue their roster and coaching staff development.

cards.headline: Spain defeats Austria 3-0 to advance in World Cup
cards.teaser: Lamine Yamal earned MVP honors as Spain beat Austria in their World Cup match at SoFi Stadium.
cards.body:
Spain defeated Austria 3-0 in their World Cup last 32 match, advancing to the next round. Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice, with Pedro Porro adding a goal in his first international appearance. Barcelona's Lamine Yamal was named the match's most valuable player after a standout performance.

The victory marks a significant milestone for Spain, securing their first knockout stage win since winning the 2010 World Cup. The team had failed to advance past the knockout rounds in the three tournaments since their last triumph. After the match, Yamal reflected on the team's progress, suggesting the tournament is now entering a critical phase.

cards.headline: Rockets sign Tari Eason to five-year, $81.5 million extension
cards.teaser: Houston retained restricted free agent Tari Eason with a long-term contract on Thursday.
cards.body:
Restricted free agent Tari Eason has agreed to a five-year, $81.5 million contract with the Houston Rockets, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. The deal keeps the 24-year-old forward with the team through the 2031 season.

The agreement represents a major commitment from Houston to Eason as part of the franchise's efforts to build around its young roster during the opening phase of NBA free agency.

cards.headline: Jaylen Brown reacts to trade from Celtics to 76ers
cards.teaser: The former Boston star expressed mixed feelings about moving to Philadelphia in a trade completed Wednesday.
cards.body:
The Boston Celtics traded 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers, receiving Paul George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks in return. Brown had expressed unhappiness with his treatment by the Celtics in the weeks leading up to the deal.

Brown said he feels both excited and disappointed about the move to the division rival. The trade reshapes both rosters during the offseason, with the 76ers immediately beginning efforts to add more star power to complement their new acquisition.

cards.headline: MLB suspends four players for roles in Red Sox-Cardinals brawl
cards.teaser: Cade Cavalli and Willson Contreras each received seven-game suspensions for the Tuesday night incident at Fenway Park.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball suspended four players Thursday for their roles in a benches-clearing brawl during Tuesday night's game at Fenway Park. Cade Cavalli and Willson Contreras each received seven-game suspensions, while Miles Mikolas was suspended for five games.

Red Sox outfielder Nate Eaton received a three-game ban for his involvement in the altercation. The fight occurred during the game between Boston and St. Louis, leading to both benches emptying onto the field. The suspensions will begin pending any appeals from the players.

cards.headline: 76ers pursue LeBron James after acquiring Jaylen Brown
cards.teaser: The Philadelphia 76ers have entered negotiations to sign LeBron James, sources told ESPN, one day after completing a trade to acquire Jaylen Brown from the Bost.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have entered negotiations to sign LeBron James one day after acquiring 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics. In the trade, Boston received Paul George, two first-round picks, and two second-round picks.

The 76ers are actively pitching James as they attempt to build a championship roster. Brown, who expressed being both excited and disappointed about the trade, joins the franchise as part of an aggressive offseason strategy aimed at contending for a title.

cards.headline: Angel Reese criticizes All-Star Game voting for Dream snubs
cards.teaser: The Chicago Sky forward called the lack of starters from the Eastern Conference-leading Atlanta Dream disrespectful.
cards.body:
Angel Reese called it "disrespectful" that the Atlanta Dream, despite leading the Eastern Conference, failed to get any players selected as starters for the WNBA All-Star Game. Reese characterized the voting results as a significant snub for the top-seeded team.

The Dream's lack of All-Star representation stood out given their strong performance and conference-leading record this season.

hero.headline: Britney Spears' Sons Make Runway Debut at Paris Fashion Week
hero.teaser: Sean Preston and Jayden James, the sons of singer Britney Spears, walked in their first fashion show during Paris Fashion Week.
hero.body:
Sean Preston and Jayden James Spears participated in runway shows during Paris Fashion Week, marking their entry into professional modeling. The brothers, whose mother is pop singer Britney Spears, appeared in shows as part of the fashion industry event in the French capital.

The young men spoke about their experience and discussed the possibility of continuing modeling careers. Britney Spears reacted to the news of her sons' participation in the fashion shows, though she has had limited public contact with them in recent years following family legal disputes.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Hold Rehearsal Dinner at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce hosted their wedding rehearsal dinner at Madison Square Garden in New York City on Thursday evening, drawing a crowd of celebrity .
cards.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce hosted a rehearsal dinner at Madison Square Garden on Thursday evening as wedding celebrations got underway in New York City. The event drew numerous celebrity guests including Jack Antonoff, Lena Dunham, Selena Gomez, Gigi Hadid, Bradley Cooper, Erin Andrews, Charissa Thompson, and Abigail Anderson.

Preparations for the festivities were visible around the Manhattan arena, with white tents being constructed and catering deliveries arriving throughout the day. The couple's choice of Madison Square Garden—typically used for concerts and sporting events—underscores the scale of their celebration during New York's Fourth of July weekend amid a heatwave.

cards.headline: Jodie Foster Criticizes Brad Pitt's F1 Film as Computer-Generated
cards.teaser: Actor Jodie Foster said the Apple film F1 starring Brad Pitt appeared to be made by artificial intelligence during a film industry discussion.
cards.body:
Jodie Foster commented on Brad Pitt's racing film F1 during a discussion with former Sony Pictures CEO Michael Lynton at the Aspen Festival. Foster suggested the film appeared to be made by AI and written by a computer, using it as an example of how technology is reshaping creative processes in Hollywood.

The conversation, titled "Who Owns the Future of Hollywood," examined industry changes and technology's growing role in filmmaking. Foster's remarks highlighted concerns about how machine involvement could affect the artistic quality of major studio productions.

cards.headline: Capitol Fourth Concert Rehearsal Closed Due to Heat
cards.teaser: Organizers closed the rehearsal for the annual Capitol Fourth concert to the public because of high temperatures in Washington.
cards.body:
The public rehearsal for A Capitol Fourth, the annual Independence Day concert at the U.S. Capitol, was closed to attendees due to heat concerns. The decision prevented spectators from watching the preparations for the July Fourth event, which airs on PBS.

Organizers are monitoring weather conditions as the holiday approaches, with extreme heat affecting outdoor events across the region. The concert itself remains scheduled to proceed as planned.

cards.headline: Ashley Tisdale Developing Comedy Series Based on Toxic Mom Drama
cards.teaser: Actor Ashley Tisdale is working with comedian Ali Wong and writer Sabrina Jalees on a Netflix comedy series.
cards.body:
Ashley Tisdale announced plans for a new Netflix comedy show being developed with Ali Wong and Sabrina Jalees. The series will draw on themes of difficult family relationships, with Tisdale describing it as exploring how people can exhibit toxic behaviors.

The project adds to Netflix's slate of comedy programming and brings together Tisdale, known for her roles in Disney Channel productions, with Wong, a stand-up comedian and actor. Production details and a release timeline have not been announced.

cards.headline: England Fans Adopt Oasis Song as World Cup Anthem
cards.teaser: English soccer fans and players have been singing Wonderwall by Oasis after matches during the FIFA World Cup tournament.
cards.body:
Wonderwall, the 1995 hit by British rock band Oasis, has become England's World Cup anthem during the 2026 tournament in the United States. Fans and players have been singing the song together following victories, establishing a new tradition this summer.

The post-match singalongs celebrate England's performances throughout the tournament, reflecting the enduring appeal of the track as a collective experience at sporting events.

cards.headline: Weezer Discusses Harder Sound on New Album
cards.teaser: Rock band Weezer released The Gold Album with a more aggressive musical approach than their recent work.
cards.body:
Weezer members Rivers Cuomo, Patrick Wilson, Brian Bell, and Scott Shriner spoke about their new album The Gold Album, describing it as having a harder edge. The band characterized the approach as less talk, more rock, indicating a shift toward a more direct musical style.

The album represents a change in direction for the veteran alternative rock group, which has released music across multiple decades. The band members discussed the creative decisions behind the record and the sound they pursued in the studio.

hero.headline: White House to launch children's investment accounts on July 4
hero.body:
The Trump administration plans to introduce investment accounts for children on July 4, positioning the initiative as a way to strengthen the financial prospects of millions of Americans under 18. The program, branded as "Trump Accounts," will be available to children who have not yet turned 18 by the end of the calendar year.

The announcement represents a significant policy move from the administration, though specific details about implementation remain limited. The White House has not yet clarified how the accounts will be funded, what investment options families can choose, or the process for accessing them. The July 4 launch date coincides with Independence Day celebrations across the country.

This federal investment account program marks a departure from existing child savings initiatives. While some states and localities have developed similar programs in recent years, this is the first nationally administered investment account program specifically designed for children.

The initiative aligns with the administration's broader push to expand wealth-building opportunities for American families. As the launch date approaches, lawmakers and policy analysts are expected to scrutinize the program's structure, including contribution limits, tax implications, and administrative oversight.

Several key questions remain unanswered about the program's design. The administration has not disclosed whether the accounts will be available universally to all eligible children or limited to families meeting certain income thresholds. Details about eligibility requirements beyond age have not been provided.

The long-term effectiveness of these accounts will depend significantly on factors the administration has not yet made public. These include initial funding amounts, potential for investment growth, and any restrictions on withdrawals before children reach adulthood.

House Democrats have criticized the timing and structure of the announcement. A 55-page report from House Democrats accuses the administration of using America's 250th birthday celebration for political gain, pointing to fundraising methods they describe as questionable. Watchdog groups have previously raised concerns about these practices.

The administration has framed the accounts as providing young Americans with a financial advantage early in life. Officials suggest the program will help build wealth among the nation's youth, though they have not yet released the detailed information necessary to assess how effectively it might achieve this goal.

Further implementation details are expected as the July 4 rollout date approaches. The administration's release of these specifics will likely shape the policy debate among lawmakers, economists, and advocacy groups interested in child welfare and financial inclusion programs.

cards.headline: Trump EPA issues guidance departing from Biden report on contaminated farmland cancer risks
cards.teaser: The Environmental Protection Agency criticized a draft Biden administration assessment on health hazards from contaminated sludge applied to farmland.
cards.body:
The Environmental Protection Agency this week issued draft guidance that criticizes a Biden administration risk assessment on health hazards from applying contaminated sludge to farmland. The Biden-era assessment had examined human health risks, including cancer, from farms contaminated with forever chemicals—persistent substances that don't break down in the environment or the body.

The new guidance reflects the Trump administration's different regulatory approach to forever chemical contamination in agricultural settings, signaling a shift in how it addresses health risks associated with these chemicals in the food supply.

cards.headline: Planned Parenthood to regain federal Medicaid funding as Republican ban expires
cards.teaser: The health care organization will regain access to federal funding on Saturday, one year after being cut off from Medicaid under Republican legislation.
cards.body:
Planned Parenthood will regain access to federal funding on Saturday, one year after Republicans cut its clinics off from Medicaid. Republicans successfully used the party-line One Big Beautiful Bill Act last year to achieve their goal of defunding Planned Parenthood.

The complicated Senate rules involved in passing that legislation meant the ban had a limited duration. The expiration of the funding prohibition returns Planned Parenthood clinics to their previous status as eligible Medicaid providers, reversing a policy change that had been a priority for Republican lawmakers.

cards.headline: Trump denies wrongdoing over cryptocurrency profits disclosed in financial forms
cards.teaser: President Trump said there was nothing illegal about the large cryptocurrency gains shown in his financial disclosure forms released this week.
cards.body:
President Trump denied any impropriety regarding substantial cryptocurrency profits shown in his recently released financial disclosure forms. In comments to CNBC, Trump stated he could have been aware of the gains but was not, and insisted there was nothing illegal about them.

According to his financial disclosures, Trump and his family earned over $1 billion last year through cryptocurrency ventures and other business interests. The scale of the digital asset returns prompted questions about the president's involvement in these transactions.

cards.headline: House Democrats accuse Trump administration of using 250th birthday celebrations for profit
cards.teaser: A report from House Democrats alleges Freedom 250 is using questionable fundraising methods tied to America's 250th anniversary celebrations.
cards.body:
House Democrats released a 55-page report accusing Freedom 250 of exploiting America's 250th anniversary celebrations through questionable fundraising methods for profit. The report examines how the Trump administration has organized the nation's birthday events.

Watchdog groups had previously raised concerns about how the celebrations were being handled. The Democratic report reinforces these criticisms, asserting that commemorative events are being leveraged for financial gain rather than serving purely patriotic purposes.

cards.headline: Louisiana attorney general indicted over alleged threats to New Orleans officials
cards.teaser: Attorney General Liz Murrill was indicted by a grand jury in connection with alleged threats against New Orleans officials, with the governor pledging a swift pardon.
cards.body:
Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill was indicted Thursday on criminal charges by a New Orleans grand jury. She is accused of attempting to intimidate local officials who opposed a Republican-enacted law to overhaul the local courts system.

Murrill allegedly told eight New Orleans officials, including Mayor Helena Moreno and District Attorney Jason Williams, that they could lose their jobs because of their opposition to the legislation. The indictment marks a significant development for the state's top law enforcement official. Governor Jeff Landry has pledged to issue a swift pardon for Murrill.

cards.headline: Mitch McConnell remains hospitalized after medical episode
cards.teaser: The former Republican majority leader is still receiving hospital care, though his office has not disclosed details of his condition or the reason for hospitalization.
cards.body:
Former Senate Republican leader Mitch McConnell remains hospitalized after experiencing a medical episode. His office confirmed he is still receiving care but has not provided details about his condition or the specific reason for the hospitalization.

McConnell, who stepped down as Republican majority leader but continues to serve in the Senate, has faced health concerns in the past. The lack of specific information about the current medical situation has left the extent of his condition unclear.
